items.prose: A hairline crack in the hermetic aluminum housing admitted ambient humidity into the NaI(Tl) crystal assembly. The hyper-hygroscopic salt dissolved into a turbid yellow chemical soup, completely extinguishing pulse height resolution for gamma spectroscopy.

Bringing the survey probe from a warm bunkhouse into a -28°C surface blizzard cleaved the CsI(Tl) crystal along (100) lattice planes. The internal optical discontinuity trapped 70% of emitted scintillation photons, cutting detector sensitivity to radioactive fallout.

Prolonged exposure to intense cobalt-60 gamma fields induced severe phosphorescent afterglow in the heavy BGO crystal. The persistent light emission saturated the photomultiplier tube base current, creating a false 500 mR/hr background baseline.

Cleaning the forty-inch plastic scintillator slab with scavenged rubbing alcohol induced catastrophic solvent crazing. Millions of micro-cracks formed across the surface, turning the crystal opaque like crushed ice and blocking scintillation photons from reaching the light guide.

Accidental exposure of the energized 1,200V photomultiplier tube to room light stripped the antimony-cesium bi-alkali photocathode layer. Quantum efficiency plummeted from 26% to zero, permanently destroying the alpha detection channel.

High geothermal heat (65°C) inside the borehole dried the silicone optical coupling grease into a powdery white residue. The refractive index mismatch created a total internal reflection barrier between the LaBr3 crystal and the PMT quartz faceplate.

A mechanical drop bent the high-permeability nickel-iron mu-metal shield surrounding the PMT. Loss of magnetic shielding allowed Earth's magnetic field to deflect the electron trajectory between dynodes 3 and 4, cutting tube gain by 45%.
